items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: The man that captured it was W.C. Handy, but it didn't belong to Handy.

ctx.x: So, see, we were doin' gospel all the time, but we wasn't knowin' that -- I mean it hadn't been labeled.

Oh, a lot of our things that we did, like the Blues was just a secular form of the spirituals. Or when -- anything like that. And like blues, "I Hate to See the Evenin' Sun Go Down", that don't belong to nobody. The man that captured it was W.C. Handy, but it didn't belong to Handy.
